exposure: indications for lower segment Caesarean sections (LSCS) (e.g., antepartum hemorrhage, fetal distress, sickle cell crisis)
outcome: neonatal outcomes (e.g., NICU admissions, requirement for observation or further care)
cohort: The study included women undergoing elective and emergency preterm Caesarean sections before 37 weeks of gestation, and their newborns, at a tertiary care teaching hospital.
finding: The audit of preterm Caesarean sections at a tertiary care center identified fetal distress, antepartum hemorrhage, and prior Caesareans as primary indications, with most women experiencing favorable obstetric profiles and stable maternal outcomes, while neonatal outcomes were multifactorial.
mod_finding: The study focused on preterm Caesarean sections, finding that 93.3% of mothers were discharged without complications, while 86.7% of newborns required NICU admission, with indications primarily being fetal distress, antepartum hemorrhage, and prior Caesareans.
